description: SIM_DEPTH_SPEC balance baselines: tools/simbot.ts (medium, plains, water 0.2), yearly rows; columns in "columns".
command: npx tsx tools/simbot.ts --size <size> --years <years> --seed <seed> --quiet  (tsx missing: bundle a driver that imports SimBot/botSystems with node_modules/.bin/rolldown --platform node --format esm --dir <out>, run with node)
notes: polish = T041 / NEW-05 final option B (taxes cost growth gradually; lead D2 sign-off under NOTE-048, confirmed signed in NOTE-050) on dev with B2: local/T041-new05-tax at ea0856d merged with dev 9ae7b28 (b2b3 and later), 128x15 s7 recorded 2026-11-10 on the desktop with tools/balance-json.ts (npx tsx tools/balance-json.ts 128 15 7 <out.json>; other lanes ran alongside, so its two timing columns are indicative only). Source parameters: wanted-weighted capped family demand mean to exponent 0.1; full R1/C0.1/I0.1; throughput bases R19/C8/I9, fraction 0.0006; exact dev tax factor through 11 percent and C1 rational tail coefficient 0.3 above 11 percent. The bot moves by design: 128x15 s7 2015 = 192,236 (b2b3 198,115: -2.97 percent, single runs; T041 on b3 was 193,831 against 192,899, +0.48 percent). The 256x60 s7 and s11 polish rows are not recorded on this tree yet (no 256x60 run at the merge: they wait for the ensemble runs), so BALANCE=256 in tests/sim/balance.test.ts has no s7 reference rows until they are. The rows signed on the old base (T041 on b3, recorded 2026-11-03: 256x60 s7 2060 = 1,511,394 against b3 1,513,835; s11 = 1,468,252 against 1,427,340) are in git history (ea0856d). Compare new work against polish; b2b3, b3, b2, b1, partB and phase0 stay.

b2b3 = WASM_PLAN B2 / WORKER_DESIGN S3 (the infra scheduler's steps in pieces with honest cost() estimates, docs/dev/B2_DESIGN.md) on dev with B3 and later: branch cloud/b2m at 99d19e9 (b2-step-split 2c4f75b merged onto dev 51ec328), recorded 2026-11-10 on the 4-core cloud box with b2work's balanceG4 = tools/balance-json.ts + a tourists column; 256x60 s7 under the timing lock with B = dev 51ec328 side by side (B reproduces every b3 row), 128x15 s7 W in the same hold; s11 not run. The headless schedule follows B2's pieces and estimates on top of B3, so the bot moves by design: 128x15 s7 2015 = 198,115 (b3 192,899; b2 on B1 193,416); 256x60 s7 2060 = 1,451,189 (b3 1,513,835). totalMsPerDay is this box's: compare against B run alongside (+1.51 on s7). Report: docs/dev/reports/local-B2-step-split.md, Cloud carry-over.

b3 = WASM_PLAN B3 / WORKER_DESIGN S4, the month-boundary work spread over the month (docs/dev/B3_DESIGN.md: tourism's venue pass on day 26, the population samples on odd days, the advisors' places predicted on day 29), on dev with B1: branch cloud/b3 at 1db0c5d (b3-month-spread merged onto dev 44f39b1), recorded 2026-11-03 with tools/balance-json.ts on the cloud box (docs/dev/reports/cloud-B3.md). The bot changes by design, from T2 and P3 alone: 128x15 s7 2015 = 192,899 (b1 196,101); 256x60 s7 2060 = 1,513,835 (b1 1,527,090), s11 = 1,427,340 (b1 1,504,571). The b1 rows reproduce on that box in every non-timing column. totalMsPerDay / econMsPerDay are the cloud box's (shared 4 cores, three runs in parallel; b1's are the desktop's): a same-session b1 run there gave 12.61 / 12.00 / 5.77 ms a day against b3's 12.42 / 11.58 / 5.78. The rows recorded before the merge (b3-month-spread 038100b on a59f08f, without B1: 128x15 s7 2015 = 195,597) are in git history (cf6af9a). Compare new work against b3; b1, partB and phase0 stay.

b2 = WASM_PLAN B2 / WORKER_DESIGN S3: the infra scheduler's steps split into pieces with honest cost() estimates (docs/dev/B2_DESIGN.md §18-19; branch b2-step-split at the fix round's final code 2c4f75b, recorded 2026-11-04 on the 4-core cloud box with b2work's balanceG4 = tools/balance-json.ts + a tourists column; 256x60 s7 under the timing lock with B = 41ae570 side by side, s11 and 128x15 s7 outside the lock, W alone at nice 19). The headless schedule follows the estimates and the pieces, so the bot moves by design: 128x15 s7 2015 = 193,416 (b1 196,101; G4 191,840); 256x60 s7 2060 = 1,509,269 (b1 1,527,090), s11 = 1,439,361 (1,504,571). totalMsPerDay is this box's: compare against B run alongside (s7 mean B 9.75, W 11.64), not against b1's desktop values; s11's and 128x15's are indicative only. Compare new work against b2; b1, partB and phase0 stay.

b1 = the services dirty trigger (T015, WASM_PLAN B1 / PI-5a; local/B1-services-trigger on bf8b6e2, recorded 2026-10-27 with tools/balance-json.ts on the desktop): passes only on coverage-relevant changes, urgent on funding / ordinances / strikes / health water / staffing / justice, a 1 s live cap. The bot moves by design: 128x15 s7 2015 = 196,101 (partB 194,432); 256x60 s7 2060 = 1,527,090 (partB 1,368,806), s11 = 1,504,571 (1,500,564). Compare new work against b1; partB and phase0 stay.

partB = final fixes, round 2 (2026-10-19, tree 4ded35c+working-tree): the WP6b round-3 balance (452b66b) plus every final-fix lane change (round 1: sim-econ, sim-traffic-save, sim-feedback, emergency; round 2: sim-feedback, emergency (EM-1 prompt scoring), sim-econ (SE-3 slice buckets, bit-identical)); the same bot command. Round 3 is superseded: after round 1 seed 7 ran -11.5 % against it at 2060 (1.369M vs 1.547M; seed 11 -4.5 %), the full-map late-game stall (lead decision 20c: no round-1 change is a bug there; F4's tree belt only moves the chaotic bot onto another layout). Compare new work against partB; phase0 stays for the spec gates (pop >= 0.9 x phase0).
preSpec = tree before any SIM_DEPTH_SPEC change (HEAD f835f06 + uncommitted audio/fireworks WIP, sim untouched).

phase0 = after the Phase 0 contract commit. Its only numeric change is P0-9 (services WORK_PER_STEP 240k -> 120k, step estimate 0.1 + 2.3 x work share), which moves scheduler step boundaries; every other Phase 0 change was verified bit-identical (128x15 run with P0-9 reverted == preSpec).
The bot is chaotic: a step-boundary change alone moves year-60 population by -9% (seed 11) / +15% (seed 7). Compare against phase0 with tolerances (spec: pop >= 0.9 x baseline) and prefer both seeds.
P0b-1 (road table reorder) intentionally changes numbers; P0b-2 re-records these baselines after it.
totalMsPerDay / econMsPerDay = CPU ms per sim day on a heavily shared 4-core box (load avg 10-25): noisy, +-20%.
